title: One apparatus, two descriptions
question: Why should changing the observer change the explanation?
recap: A moving conductor in a magnetic field and a moving magnet near a conductor invite different classical explanations. Relativity asks for consistent predictions of the same physical arrangement, not identical numerical field components.
premises: Compare inertial descriptions of the same apparatus and events.
The relativity principle and light-speed postulate are stated physical assumptions.
limitations: A simulator cannot prove its own postulates.
The restricted dipole-and-conductor model does not cover every induction experiment.

overview.text: A moving conductor in a magnetic field and a moving magnet near a conductor invite different classical explanations. Relativity asks for consistent predictions of the same physical arrangement, not identical numerical field components.

full.text: In one description, charges move through a magnetic field. In another, the conductor is at rest and an electric field drives them. The apparent explanatory asymmetry motivates the paper; it is not resolved by declaring that electric and magnetic fields have the same values for every observer.

The two postulates state that the laws have the same form in inertial frames and that light propagates in vacuum at a definite speed independent of the source motion. They are the starting point, not consequences of failed ether-drift experiments alone.

The magnet-and-conductor laboratory compares the descriptions under explicit transformations. At finite relative speed, forces and electromotive quantities must be compared through their transformation laws. The familiar equal-value argument is only a low-speed approximation.

full.returnCaption: Return to why should changing the observer change the explanation.

items: Identify the conductor, magnet, charges, and the observer.
Describe the same interaction in the other inertial frame.
Record which quantities change under that change of description.
State the two postulates before using them.
Return to §6 to see electric and magnetic components transform together.

margin.text: This is a modern explanatory reconstruction. It neither quotes the opening paragraphs as a translation nor turns the absence of detected ether drift into a deductive proof of the postulates.
